svg.title: Allocate startup cash before buying volume
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-07-startup-capital-allocation; chart type: stacked_comparison; title: Allocate startup cash before buying volume; subtitle: Four buckets total $8,000 lean, $30,000 working, or $45,000 expanded.; chapter number: 4; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: Numeric values display the $30,000 working plan. Each detail also states its lean and expanded allocations. Lean allocations sum to $8,000; expanded allocations sum to $45,000. These are startup cash allocations, not annual expense deductions or additional revenue.; caption: Do not count an unspent reserve as an expense. Release test capital in small cohorts, and resize settlement float using observed buyer collections rather than invoice due dates alone.; stages: label: Routing and evidence setup; value: $3,500 working allocation for initial systems; numeric value: 3500.0; detail: Lean $1,000; working $3,500; expanded $5,000. Fund telephone numbers, initial Ringba or Retreaver configuration, evidence integration, landing-page instrumentation, and test-call fixtures before connecting paid traffic.; label: Contracts and operating setup; value: $4,500 working allocation for documented counterparties; numeric value: 4500.0; detail: Lean $1,000; working $4,500; expanded $7,000. Fund buyer and publisher contract work, jurisdiction-specific advertising review, accounting setup, recording procedures, and written acceptance and dispute definitions.; label: Controlled acquisition experiments; value: $14,000 working allocation for measured traffic cohorts; numeric value: 14000.0; detail: Lean $4,000; working $14,000; expanded $21,000. Release media or publisher test spending in capped increments. Stop a source when realized contribution or evidence quality breaches its documented operating threshold.; label: Settlement float and contingency; value: $8,000 working allocation for timing and reversals; numeric value: 8000.0; detail: Lean $2,000; working $8,000; expanded $12,000. Reserve cash for prepaid acquisition, buyer payment delays, and reversals. Base acquisition averages about $1,047.95 daily; seven days consumes about $7,335.62 before other obligations, making an $8,000 reserve tight.

rect.title: label: Routing and evidence setup; numeric value: 3500.0; value: $3,500 working allocation for initial systems; detail: Lean $1,000; working $3,500; expanded $5,000.
